That is not a detail bolted onto the design; at these sizes it is likely to be the      design's largest cost. A Q32 value is eight bytes and a storage slot is      thirty-two, so four values pack into a slot and a 1024-wide residual stream is 256      slots. Writing a slot that was previously zero costs 22,100 gas, so one checkpoint      of the residual stream alone is about 5.7M \u2014 against roughly 690k for the layer      that produced it.      The cache is worse and unavoidable. Each layer contributes `kvWidth` values per      position, they cannot be recomputed without redoing every earlier position, and      they must outlive the transaction because the next token reads them.
